title: Sales enablement playbook — positioning, competitive briefs, pricing, case studies, security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's sales-facing positioning, battlecards, competitive brief guidance, pitch deck checklist, pricing guidance, reproducible case study templates, and a customer-facing Security FAQ. Use this as the single source-of-truth for SDRs, AEs, solutions engineers, and GTM enablement content.

Audience: sales reps, solutions engineering, customer success, channel partners.

Owner & maintenance
- Document owner: Go-to-market Enablement (owner: Asha Patel)
- Review cadence: quarterly (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4) or on major product/security changes
- Where assets live: Redwood Sales Drive > Decks (internal) and Confluence attachments for canonical slide decks and battlecards

1) Core positioning and messaging (elevator + 3-minute pitch)

Elevator pitch (15–25s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — letting engineering teams ship LLM features without building or owning large-scale inference infra.

3-minute pitch (structure):
1. Problem (30s) — Serving LLMs in production is expensive, brittle, and operationally heavy: model throughput/latency variance, unpredictable costs, and complex infra (GPU, networking, KV cache).
2. Solution (60s) — Redwood provides a unified runtime, smart routing, and deployment abstraction (hosted, dedicated, private) with tooling for cost/perf control (batching, caching, quantization).
3. Differentiators (45s) — Production-first telemetry and rollouts, predictable economics (Dedicated/reserved capacity), private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations, and built-in graceful degradation.
4. Proof & ask (45s) — Pilot on hosted API or reserved Dedicated pool; offer to run a three-week POC with defined success criteria (latency targets, cost per token reduction, and error budget).

Key value props mapped to buyer personas
- Developer / Platform engineer: Simple API, SDKs, deterministic performance, and infra portability.
- ML engineer: Model catalog, quantization profiles, eval tooling to prevent regression.
- Product/Revenue lead: Predictable cost, SLA-backed Dedicated capacity, and faster time-to-market.
- Security/Compliance: Private deployment, audit logs, KMS/HSM, SOC2 & ISO alignment.

Messaging dos and don'ts
- DO emphasize engineering ownership reduction (we run inference, you ship features).
- DO quantify impact when possible (latency p95, cost per 1K tokens, SLA).
- DON'T oversell model accuracy improvements — focus on serving and operational guarantees.
- DON'T conflate hosted convenience with suitability for regulated workloads (reference Private/Dedicated options).

2) Competitive brief templates (one-pagers)

Purpose: Equip reps with short, repeatable comparisons vs. common competitors (cloud-managed endpoints, LLM API providers, inference infra vendors). Each brief should contain: 1) Summary; 2) Feature matrix; 3) Typical customer profile; 4) How to win (talking points); 5) Traps/objections; 6) Suggested demo hooks.

Feature comparison matrix (example columns):
- Capability: Unified API, Dedicated/reserved capacity, Private (VPC/on-prem), Model catalog, Quantization recommendations, Telemetry & per-token cost breakdown, Rollouts & canaries, SLA.
- Redwood: yes/yes/yes/curated/yes/first-class/yes/99.9%
- Cloud-managed endpoint: yes/no/limited/no/no/basic/limited/varies
- Inference vendor X: integration-focused/yes/possible/no/partial/no/partial/none

How to win (example bullets):
- Emphasize code parity across hosted/dedicated/private — reduces friction for platform teams who need to standardize.
- Stress cost controls: batching, KV caching, quantization profiles, and Dedicated reservations drive measurable cost reductions vs pay-as-you-go alternatives.
- Mobilize SEs to benchmark P95 and throughput during POC; show our telemetry and cost breakdown dashboards.

Common objections and counters
- "We can run open-source models ourselves": Counter with run cost + operational complexity math — show typical TCO and mean time to recovery (MTTR) benefits. Offer a side-by-side benchmark.
- "We need guarantees for compliance": Point to Private deployment options, KMS integrations, audit logs, and enterprise support packages.
- "Latency concerns for high-throughput workloads": Reference Dedicated/pinned pools, autoscaling policies, and observed p95 numbers from benchmarks.

3) Pitch deck checklist & winning demo flow

Canonical deck structure (recommended 10–12 slides):
1. Title / one-liner (with customer logo if allowed)
2. The problem — real world example
3. Redwood solution overview (runtime + platform)
4. Deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) + decision guidance
5. Performance & cost evidence (benchmarks)
6. Security & compliance (SOC2, ISO, VPC, audit logs)
7. Customer case studies / ROI numbers
8. Implementation & timeline (POC → pilot → production)
9. Pricing & commercial options
10. Next steps / success criteria / contacts

Demo flow (30–40 minutes total):
- 5m: Quick intro & agenda
- 10m: Live demo — show API request → streaming response, telemetry dashboard, model rollouts
- 10m: Deep dive (for SE): Dedicated pool config, autoscaling, KV caching settings, and quantization recommendation results
- 5–10m: Q&A & next steps

Assets to keep updated
- Canonical slide deck (Sales Drive): filename "Redwood_Inference_Sales_Deck_Master.pptx"
- Demo scripts & reproducible notebooks (SE repo)
- One-page battlecards per competitor (Confluence attachments)

4) Pricing guidance (commercial primer)

Pricing model summary (high level):
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token generation, per-embedding), free tier / trial credits, list & discounting bands for volume commitments.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity (GPU-hour equivalent) with burst pricing and predictable unit economics.
- Private: licensing + support (on-prem or VPC), professional services for installation and integration.

How to position pricing in conversations
- For SMB / developer-first customers: start with Hosted API; highlight fast time-to-value and pay-as-you-grow model.
- For scale / predictable spend customers: recommend Dedicated; emphasize SLA-backed latency/uptime and cost predictability via reservations.
- For regulated workloads: Private + Professional Services; lead with security controls and auditability.

Discounting guardrails (playbook guidance):
- Standard discount bands by ARR/commitment (example): 3–10% for small ARR, 10–25% for mid-market commits, 25%+ for enterprise multi-year commitments (confirm with RevOps).
- No unilateral commitments for infrastructure or custom integrations without Sales Ops / Legal approval.

Commercial asks / trial structure
- Pilot offer template: 3–4 week pilot, defined SLOs (p95 latency target, throughput goal, cost-per-1K-token baseline), technical success criteria, and exec sponsor alignment.

5) Case study template & quick wins

One-page case study structure (reproducible)
- Title: Customer + short outcome (e.g., "Acme reduced inference cost by 38% while improving p95 latency")
- Customer profile: industry, company size, deployment mode used
- Problem statement & impact metrics pre-engagement
- Solution summary (what we delivered: model, deployment mode, config)
- Results (quantitative): latency p95, throughput, cost per 1K tokens, error rates, deployment time
- Key quotes & contacts (with customer permission)
- Implementation timeline & next steps

Quick wins to recommend in pilots
- Enable KV/prefix caching for repeat traffic to cut token costs 15–40%
- Apply recommended quantization profile for non-critical models to reduce GPU memory by 40%
- Configure burst and autoscale policies to handle diurnal traffic without large reservations

6) Security FAQ for prospects (top-line answers for initial conversations)

Q: What compliance certifications does Redwood have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II readiness, is pursuing ISO 27001 certification, and supports enterprise evidence packages on request. (Contact Security for the latest attestation artifacts.)

Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC/on-prem?
A: Yes. Private deployments provide a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package for regulated or air-gapped environments. Professional services can handle install and validation.

Q: How is customer data protected at rest and in transit?
A: All customer traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3 encrypted in transit. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. For Private deployments, customers can bring their KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) integrations.

Q: Who has access to my data and logs?
A: Hosted API: access is restricted to Redwood SRE/Platform engineers on a least-privilege basis; audit logs and access review processes are maintained. Dedicated & Private: customer-admins control access and RBAC can be integrated with the customer's identity provider.

Q: Do you support data residency requirements?
A: Yes. Hosted API offers region selection for data residency in supported regions; For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments located in the desired geography.

Q: How do you handle incident response and notifications?
A: Redwood maintains an incident response playbook, customer incident notification SLAs for enterprise customers, and an on-call SRE rota. For Dedicated/Private customers, we provide runbooks and can coordinate on-call handoffs.

Q: Can we audit model access and inference logs?
A: Yes — audit logging is available. We provide token-level telemetry, request/response metadata (with options to redact content), and exportable logs for SIEM ingestion.

Q: What are the SLAs for Dedicated and Hosted?
A: Example SLAs (subject to contract): Dedicated: 99.9% uptime with latency targets defined per pool; Hosted: best-effort SLA with billing credits for major outages (see commercial terms). Always refer to the approved contract template for exact terms.
